#1508. Leeds transfer news: Will Lankshear January hopes shot down by 44-goal striker

By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33

Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.

The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.

Lankshear netted the winner as Middlesbrough beat Swansea City 2-1 on Tuesday night, a result that saw Kim Hellberg's men move one point clear of Wolverhampton Wanderers at the top of the Championship table.

The 21-year-old unsurprisingly sits top of the Championship top scorers charts, three clear of closest challenger Andri Gudjohnsen of Blackburn Rovers in the race for the Golden Boot.

Lankshear's form has inevitably led to speculation surrounding a swift return to the Premier League, with multiple clubs believed to be interested in securing his services, including Leeds.

Former club Tottenham, Arsenal, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United have also been credited with an interest, although Middlesbrough's £70m asking price could deter suitors.

Now, former Leeds forward Deane - who scored 44 goals in 199 matches for the Whites - has expressed his view that Lankshear should remain at the Riverside Stadium over the winter.

“This is his breakout season, and he is at a good club," Deane told Sports Mole. "Middlesbrough look on course to challenge for promotion, so hopefully he gets there with them.

“He will be ambitious and attract attention from clubs such as Leeds, Brighton and Newcastle. He would be a good addition to a squad. But for his own development, I think he is in a good place at Middlesbrough.”

Lankshear made just six senior appearances for Tottenham before being sold in a £9.8m deal over the summer, and the striker's contract with Middlesbrough does not expire until 2031.

A young striker scoring for fun in the Championship will always attract glances from top-tier clubs, but Lankshear may struggle to force his way into Daniel Farke's first XI right now.

First-choice pairing Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor boast a respectable nine Premier League goals between them in 2026-27, and as long as both are fit, they will spearhead Farke's 3-5-2 system.

Calvert-Lewin is now in the final 24 months of his contract at Elland Road, but the England international is understood to be close to signing a new Leeds deal.

Lukas Nmecha also provides a steady backup option, although he is due to become a free agent in 2027 and may seek a move away in January if his game-time situation does not improve.

However, Nmecha's proposed exit would then open the door for summer signing Jean-Matteo Bahoya to earn more opportunities, so a winter move for Lankshear would make little sense for all involved.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

“I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

At Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

In this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

This is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

So far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

These numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”

Who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.

#1504. Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026

Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.

Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.

The joint bid projected that the competition would attract 3.5billion viewers worldwide. And that 4.5m tickets would be sold across the host nations.

But the key for Scotland will be the impact it has on girls taking up the sport, supporters watching it and professionals playing it north of the Border.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir has already described it as a ‘pivotal’ moment, a ‘real opportunity’ to drive momentum and reach another level, domestically and internationally.

She’s right. It is an opportunity, of the once-in-a-lifetime variety, but a word of caution is in order. Opportunities are not enough in themselves to be transformative.

They have to be embraced, exploited and squeezed for all they are worth so that every last drop of their potential is properly fulfilled.

Star player Caroline Weir believes co-hosting the World Cup could be pivotal for women's football in Scotland

It would be criminal if the powers-that-be got complacent about this priceless gift and made assumptions about its long-term legacy.

More players, more fans and more media coverage would be hugely exciting, but it will all be wasted if not supported by facilities, coaches and the safeguarding that goes with it.

It has happened before. Interest in athletics rocketed after Glasgow 2014, but a poor infrastructure, which continued to rely on volunteers, prevented a grassroots boom.

And how many times have we heard Judy Murray complain that Scottish tennis squandered the opportunity presented to it by her son, Andy?

Scotland’s women played at the World Cup in 2019. Their game has grown since then, but the national side have not been to another major tournament and the domestic product is still a shadow of its English counterpart.

Only a handful of Scottish teams have full-time players. The wages are way behind those on offer down south. And professional men’s clubs could do much, much more to develop the sport. It’s no wonder the Scottish league can’t keep its better players.

The opposite is true in England, where the success of the national team is often attributed to the level of investment by the FA and the backing of sponsors across the country.

The good news is that Scotland have made a start on that front with something called Project 2035, which aims to transform girls' and women’s football over the next decade.

The Scottish government has stumped up an initial £250,000 to help with the 10-year plan, which outlined a number of key objectives earlier this month.

They want to grow participation at grassroots level, increase the number of women working in football - as coaches, leaders and decision-makers - and quadruple the number of fans. The hope also is that Scotland will progress beyond the group stage of at least one World Cup by 2035.

Having those ambitions is one thing; making good on them is quite another. The government, the league, clubs and the ruling body: all should be thrilled by this opportunity but they should also feel the pressure that it brings. For it is their responsibility, their duty, to make the most of it.

#1502. Aston Villa news: Why Unai Emery's immunity from criticism should no longer exist

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:36

Such is Unai Emery's status at Aston Villa that few would be surprised if the redeveloped North Stand, when completed in 2027, is named after the Spaniard.

Taking Villa from relegation candidates in 2022-23 to two Champions League qualifications and a Europa League trophy by the conclusion of 2025-26 arguably deserves that level of recognition.

However, despite the expectation that a contract extension past 2029 will be penned in the near future, it will not necessarily strengthen Emery's, or the club's, position in the long term.

Tuesday's 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray extended Villa's recent winless streak across all competitions to six matches. They have failed to score in four of those games, and given up leads on three occasions.

Emery is no stranger to an extended blip in form. At the start of both 2025-26 and 2026-27, Villa were off the pace. It is to Emery's credit that Villa became brief Premier League title contenders in a matter of months and still finished in fourth position in last season's standings.

Nevertheless, Villa are now enduring their second extended winless period of the season, raising the question of whether the West Midlands outfit are experiencing a blip or a gradual decline under their most successful manager for nearly 45 years?

With 116 wins from 215 matches, silverware, and delivering moments and experiences that will last a lifetime, Emery is etched into the Villa history books as a God.

At the same time, this is now a manager of a team that has only recorded 11 wins from his last 27 games in all competitions, as well as losing on 10 occasions. Just seven wins have come from 19 fixtures in 2026-27.

When Villa defeated Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Manchester City in relatively quick succession with performances that mixed grit, shrewdness and attacking vigour, the conclusion was that Emery's new-looked team had flicked a switch.

However, Villa have regressed as quickly as they had seemingly improved. When you take into account that Villa had one win in seven between February 1 and March 4, and lost three in a row between April 25 and May 3, this is now the fourth "blip" in less than nine months.

Some of the aforementioned statistics will be comparable with managers at similarly-sized clubs in the Premier League and Europe, yet that usually leads to scrutiny over the job that has been conducted over a specific period. Not talk of a contract until 2030 and beyond being signed.

By modern-day standards, Emery is in the unique position of having high control over which players are signed and sold. He essentially has the keys to the footballing side of the club and Villa's fate on the pitch is solely in his hands.

Yet, a 12-time trophy-winning manager of a team that has only earned fewer Premier League points than Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool across a four-year period is frequently telling the media, or anyone who will listen, that Villa should not be competing in the top six, nor for the top-eight positions in the league phase of the Champions League.

Is this an example of Emery trying to reinforce the perception that Villa are underdogs to the so-called Premier League 'big six' because of what is, admittedly, a scandalous PSR scenario, or is it a pre-orchestrated approach to defend his position whenever results do not go Villa's way?

Staying on the subject of things being pre-orchestrated, not enough scrutiny is coming over Villa's and Emery's use of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott and Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho.

Since the summer of 2025, Villa have included £35m and, allegedly, £43m fees with those clubs to sign the players in question should they achieve a specific appearance threshold. Between them, they have made three starts and 13 substitute outings when spending the majority of the time available for selection.

On Tuesday night, Emery omitted Garnacho - who has accumulated fewer than 100 minutes across seven substitute appearances - from the squad for the Galatasaray match, despite naming one fewer substitute than was permitted. Afterwards, he delivered a frank response over the Argentine's chances of earning future game time.

If Villa do not want to pay vast amounts of money for players, they do not have to. However, are Villa not harming their chances of signing players through similar deals in the future? Why should clubs trust such deals to go through if Emery is choosing not to select such players or is being told not to?

Everything points to Garnacho becoming Elliott 2:0 and the situation deserves some clarity. If an honest assessment cannot be delivered to fans and the media, Emery leaves himself open to persistent questioning and criticism, and it will be warranted.

Of course, the evolving Garnacho saga can change for the better. Excluding Villa's game against Chelsea in December, the winger has seven more chances to feature in 2026.

There can be a rapid upturn in fortunes, too. Villa face Ipswich Town, Everton and Crystal Palace in the Premier League before they welcome Paris Saint-Germain to Villa Park in the Champions League.

However, when Emery is storming down tunnels before the full-time whistle, throwing tantrums in the media and getting increasingly frustrated on the touchline as his team look slow, devoid of ideas and can make 700 passes in a game and not score against a team such as Sunderland, it can be argued that Villa need a change of direction rather than remaining on their current path.

Villa have a deep squad with talent that can earn them success in the future, yet they have too many under-performers or players who may simply be tired even at this stage of the season. Whether that is down to Emery, or too much emphasis being placed on players needing to adapt to the "Emery way" before they earn regular starts, it is open to debate.

Regardless, Villa are currently on a downward trajectory under his leadership, and Emery has questions to answer if he is to remain untouchable at a club that want to hand him a contract extension when they could enter December with just three Premier League wins in 2026-27.

#1500. Report: Chelsea's attempt to ruin Liverpool transfer plan revealed

Liverpool's biggest need in the upcoming transfer window is a midfielder.

The Reds have enjoyed a fairly strong start to life under Andoni Iraola, but strengthening the midfield would transform them into legitimate title contenders.

#1499. Venezia vs. Bologna - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 12:37

Venezia head into their matchday 13 encounter with in-form Bologna seeking a third league victory in four matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo.

The Europe-chasing visitors sit 11 places above the Veneto-based club in the Serie A table but will be wary of the Winged Lions' recent improvement in front of their supporters.

On the surface, Venezia's decision to replace Giovanni Stroppa with Davide Nicola has made little difference to their results, with the Lagunari sitting bottom of the league.

However, a closer look suggests that the home supporters can expect a battling performance when Bologna travel to Venice on Friday.

Still the only Serie A side yet to draw this term, the promoted outfit have suffered 10 defeats in 12 matches, including four since Nicola's appointment in October.

Nonetheless, all six of their points have come from their last three matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo, where they have beaten Napoli (1-0) and Udinese (2-1) either side of a 2-0 defeat to Inter Milan.

That loss to the defending champions came courtesy of own goals from Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal in the final 10 minutes, with the bottom-placed side attempting 12 shots to Inter's 16 and creating two clear-cut chances to the Nerazzurri's three.

Although three matches represent a small sample, those recent performances in Venice suggest that the Lagunari are slowly turning the tide at home, giving Bologna reason for caution ahead of Friday's trip.

Raffaele Palladino's Rossoblu know all about upturns in form, having experienced their own resurgence since Domenico Tedesco was dismissed in mid-September following a winless start to the campaign.

A 1-0 defeat to Napoli at the Maradona proved the final straw for the hierarchy in Bologna, with Palladino inheriting a Felsinei side that had collected just one point from an available 12 across four matches.

Sitting 16th at the time and outside the bottom three only on goal difference, the Rossoblu have since collected 17 points from a possible 24 under Palladino to climb to ninth on 18 points, just three behind sixth-placed Juventus.

Only Lazio (22), AC Milan (19) and Roma (18) have earned more points during that period, underlining Bologna's resurgence since Tedesco's departure as they target a sixth victory in nine league matches.

The travelling supporters will therefore back their in-form side to overcome Nicola's men, although the result may be less straightforward than some anticipate given the Lagunari's steady improvement on home turf.

Toma Basic (muscle), Thierry Correia (thigh), Pasquale Mazzocchi (muscle), Andrea Adorante (hernia), Marin Sverko (hip) and Bartol Franjic (shoulder) are all considered unlikely to feature in gameweek 13.

No player has scored more than twice for the division's lowest scorers, with Akor Adams and Antoine Hainaut netting two apiece to account for half of the Winged Lions' eight league goals.

While Bologna have no individual producing spectacular numbers, they boast a broader spread of match-winners, with Federico Bernardeschi, Samuel Mbangula, Riccardo Orsolini and Tommaso Pobega all scoring twice.

Although Juan Miranda, Nicolo Cambiaghi and Jens Odgaard have yet to score, their respective returns of five, three and two assists underline their importance to the Rossoblu.

However, Bologna must manage without Miranda, who is sidelined alongside Jay Enem (Achilles), Oussama El Azzouzi (thigh) and Emil Holm (thigh).

Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Juan Jesus; Hainaut, Kike Perez, Sohm, Busio, Haps; Lauberbach, Adams

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Cambiaghi; Bernardeschi, Orsolini; Odgaard

Venezia's victories over Napoli and Udinese suggest that their lowly position does not tell the whole story, particularly after they made Inter work for their points in Venice.

However, Bologna's 17-point return from eight matches under Palladino reflects a more sustained improvement, and the visitors should have enough attacking variety to edge Friday's encounter.

#1498. Kevin De Bruyne insists potential punishment over Man City's guilty verdict will not tarnish his old club's achievements under Pep Guardiola - or diminish his 'love' for the owners

Published: 16:01 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:04 EST, 23 November 2026

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne insisted that any potential punishment for breaching financial rules will not change what Pep Guardiola’s team achieved and their memories of success.

The Belgian was a key pillar during the spell of unprecedented domestic dominance and has a statue commissioned outside the Etihad Stadium.

De Bruyne is back in town with Napoli for Tuesday’s Champions League tie, reiterating his ‘love’ for City and its owners, while revealing recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

The 35-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal and were sanctioned after being found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them.

De Bruyne’s trophy haul – six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups and five Carabao Cups – were largely secured outside of the nine-year period in which City were scrutinised, up to 2018.

‘I’m proud of what I've done as a football player,’ De Bruyne said. ‘Honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football (with them), I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything.

The 36-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal

‘It (stripping of titles) still doesn't change (anything), my football has not changed. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

‘But everybody has his own opinion and other people may be disgraced a bit. I can't change anything about that.’

De Bruyne’s final two seasons at City were plagued by injury before he joined Napoli on a free transfer in 2025 and his first return in last year’s Champions League lasted just 26 minutes as he hobbled off.

Classed as the greatest player in the club’s modern history, De Bruyne was typically forthright on the uncertainty surrounding his former employers after the guilty verdicts read by a three-person independent commission.

‘My feelings have never been different,’ he added. ‘Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

‘Of course, it's a lot of things that have been going on. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change. Even now, the people who treated me and my family for 10 years is the most important thing.’

De Bruyne left City under duress, vehemently disagreeing with the club’s decision not to offer him a new contract following a spate of injuries before choosing Napoli – and his long-term future in Serie A is now appearing in doubt.

All eyes in Italy were on the midfielder’s public response to an interview published with his wife, Michele, in which she was reported to have criticised life in Naples and yearned for a move away. Those comments were taken out of context, according to a visibly frustrated De Bruyne, with PSV Eindhoven looking at securing a transfer in January.

De Bruyne left City under duress but revealed recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak

But City supporters will have been more interested in how far De Bruyne went in backing their club ahead of next month’s appeal hearing.

‘In life there are rules, but everybody plays to the limit, I would say,’ he claimed, seemingly referring to how financial rules are interpreted by the Premier League’s elite clubs.

‘I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams.

‘So for me that's the thing that I value most. The most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things, and I've given my all.’

De Bruyne smirked as he discussed how he knew exactly how City would attack Napoli given his knowledge of the club and manager Enzo Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2023 Treble campaign.

Maresca is facing criticism after three defeats and a draw in their last four league games. The Italian called for calm over recent performances and believes that the transition from Guardiola was always going to represent a bumpy road.

‘It's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method,’ Maresca said.

‘It's not easy to all of a sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs.’

Arsenal switch to their right and try to free Saka but Trafford comes out to kick it into touch.

#1496. Watch: Amorim’s passionate ‘biggest mistake’ response which achieved viral status

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he said.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your plan. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear plan, don’t look at the table.

“Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

“So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

“Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear plan what to do.”

#1495. Levante vs Racing de Santander - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 12:48, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 12:50

Racing de Santander will be bidding to continue their excellent run of form when they head to Estadi Ciutat de Valencia on Friday evening to tackle Levante.

Levante just about lead the overall head-to-head record between these two sides, winning 11 of their 30 meetings in all competitions, suffering 10 defeats in the process.

Levante have a record of two wins, six draws and five defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them down in 15th spot in the La Liga table.

The Frogs have been an entertaining watch at home this season, scoring 14 times and conceding 13, boasting a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Luis Castro's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-1 draw with Elche, while they also drew 0-0 with Celta Vigo before the November international break, with their last victory coming at home to Athletic Bilbao on October 21.

Levante finished 16th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27, but they have found it difficult to win matches so far this term.

The Frogs actually beat Racing 3-1 in the last match between the two teams in April 2025, but two of their last four meetings have been won by the latter.

Racing, who are the reigning Segunda Division champions, have been one of the stories of the season in Spain's top flight, impressing hugely on their return to La Liga.

The Green and Whites boast a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats from their 13 league matches, which has left them seventh in the table on 17 points.

Jose Alberto's side have actually conceded 32 times in La Liga this season, which is comfortably the worst record in the division, but they have found the back of the net on 20 occasions - the sixth-best attacking record at this stage.

Racing will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Real Sociedad, and they have now been victorious in three of their last four in the league, and four of their last five in all competitions.

The Green and Whites have struggled away from home this season, though, losing five of their six league matches, only managing to pick up three points.

Racing de Santander form (all competitions):

Levante lost Jeremy Toljan to an injury in the early stages of their clash with Elche last time out, and the defender is set to miss out on Friday.

The hosts have not reported any further problems, so aside from Nacho Perez coming in for Toljan at right-back, it could be the same side that started the team's last game.

Roger Brugue has scored five times and registered one assist in 13 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set for a spot in the starting side.

Karl Etta Eyong, though, is likely to start on the bench.

As for Racing, Maguette Gueye, Alvaro Mantilla and Andres Martin could potentially miss the match through injury, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape.

Yassir Zabiri, who is on loan at the club from Rennes, has been in excellent form this season, scoring 11 times in 13 league appearances, and he will again feature in the final third of the field.

There should also be another spot in the first XI for the experienced Sergio Canales, who has been a key player for the club this term at the age of 35, coming up with two goals and one assist in 13 appearances.

Bayern Munich have some of the best attacking talent in the world.

#1493. Next Lincoln City manager: Chris Cohen, Tom Shaw sacked by Championship club

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:59, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 12:59

Lincoln City have sacked co-managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

The pair were promoted from the club's backroom staff after head coach Michael Skubala made the decision to leave the League One champions for Bristol City in the summer.

With Lincoln sitting in 21st place in the Championship table and two points above the relegation zone, a positive spin can be put on the club's first campaign in the second tier of English football for more than 60 years.

However, Tuesday's 4-0 defeat at Charlton Athletic was Lincoln's fifth successive loss in the Championship.

As well as one win and eight defeats being posted across a 10-match period, the club's hierarchy have decided for a change in direction.

A statement read: "We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division.”   "We know how much this football club means to our supporters and are humbled by the level of support we’ve had home and away so far this season."

ℹ️ City can confirm Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw have been relieved of their duties as head coaches with immediate effect. We thank them for their contributions to the club over the last several years and wish them well for the future. https://t.co/mwLolWdxhp

Lincoln add that they will next provide an update on their search for a successor to Cohen and Shaw on November 30.

Despite 15 points coming from 17 matches, Cohen and Shaw can have no complaints over Lincoln's decision.

With Preston North End and Burnley - in 22nd and 23rd position - closing the gap, Lincoln's owners are justified in the move that they have taken.

Furthermore, second-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers are the next visitors to the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Likely viewing that game as a free-hit under first-team coach Stuart Pearson, Lincoln will look to have a permanent manager in place for the trip to Cardiff City on December 5.

#1491. Opinion: Liverpool prepare for major tactical shift as new long-term target emerges

Andoni Iraola has now managed to get Liverpool to fourth in the Premier League table.

Obviously, this is still miles away from where they need to be but, the fact that only seven points separate them and first-placed Arsenal is excellent news.

Right now, it's unclear where Liverpool are going to finish in England's top flight but, if they keep performing to the standard they showed on Sunday against Manchester United, they'll be storming their way up the table.

But, for them to do this, improvements need to be made to their squad as, all of their other title rivals will be adding extra firepower to their ranks.

So, the fact that the January transfer window is now just over a month away is rather exciting.

Especially with all the players that they've just been linked with.

Liverpool see Gustavo Varela as a 'long-term target'

Liverpool have several problem areas among their ranks that need addressing.

Obviously, since they're one of the biggest clubs in the world, they won't have any problem finding players who want to join.

However, the prices that Premier League clubs have to pay instantly have extra money added on top of them.

That's why only a certain number of deals can be struck by Liverpool in each window.

Moves for the future are also laid out with a new update from Football Insider sharing that the Reds' recent links with Monza striker Gustavo Varela are for the 'long-term' rather than the short-term.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform."

Liverpool's interest in Gustavo Varela could mean that they're changing to a two striker formation

Liverpool only have two fit strikers among their ranks at the moment.

Alexander Isak is one of them and, since he was the Reds' record signing, he's obviously going to be Iraola's striker.

Lewis Koumas is the other and, even though his manager likes him, the fact that Hugo Ekitike is edging closer to a return will certainly worry him.

Before he got injured last term, Ekitike was easily Liverpool's best player and, they probably wouldn't have qualified for the Champions League if it wasn't for him.

So, the fact that Varela is now emerging as a potential option for the Reds on their shortlist certainly raises a few questions.

The easiest explanation for this move would be that, eventually, Iraola wants to move to a two striker formation while having Varela and Koumas as his back-up options.

Obviously, there are now guarantees that this will play out like that but, if that is the case, a major tactical change could be on its way to Anfield in the next couple of years.

#1489. The Women's World Cup is coming home... but 2035 cannot be treated as a fix for the game's problems, writes TARA ANSON-WALSH

Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026

The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.

Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.

Over in Zurich, FIFA president Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup, describing a time when they 'didn't exist'.

'We all remember the last Women's World Cup,' the embattled 56-year-old Italian said, calling it 'a huge success'.

The irony, of course, is that the last Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand is remembered by many for all the wrong reasons, with newspaper back pages peppered with images of Spain captain Jenni Hermoso's kiss with the former president of Spain's FA, Luis Rubiales, for days after the final.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England in Sydney.

Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England

There is an added layer of irony in that Infantino had, two days before the 2023 final, angered many women worldwide with yet another controversial speech in which he told them: 'You have the power to change', but that they had to 'convince us men what we have to do'.

Alongside this patronising statement, Infantino also insisted that equal pay at the World Cup 'would not solve anything'.

Three years later, Infantino is unfortunately still at the helm, while UEFA's attempts to unseat him following his controversial bid to sell off the World Cup now look to have failed spectacularly, with the football despot increasingly likely to secure a fourth term.

What the social and political landscape will look like by the time this women's footballing bonanza arrives on these shores in 2035 remains unclear. What is clear, however, is that the game's continued progress will require more than the record attendances and soaring commercial revenues the FA are predicting.

It will require the figures who have too often held it back to finally step aside, and that process should begin with the likes of Infantino being shown the door.

It will require those at the top of English football to put their heads together and work out how to stem falling attendances in the league. The average attendance across the first eight WSL matchweeks of 2024-25 was 8,173. Last season it was 7,472. This season, it is tracking at around 5,677.

And third, it will require somewhere other than Wembley to stage the final.

Wembley was, of course, the scene of Chloe Kelly's moment of madness, yet by the time the 2035 Women's World Cup comes around it will also have hosted the men's finals of Euro 2024 and 2028.

The FA paid off its debt on the national stadium in 2024, 17 years after its reopening, and is no longer obligated to host major events there to service repayments.

The rules have been left open for another venue to emerge to host the final, such as Man United's proposed new 100,000 stadium

While under current FIFA regulations, Wembley is the only one of the proposed 22 stadiums that meets the requirements to host a final, the rules have been left open enough for another venue to emerge should a suitable stadium be completed before 2035.

Step up Sir Jim Ratcliffe, although please refer back to point one in this regard – the Manchester United co-owner who famously asked former captain Katie Zelem 'what do you do here?' while touring the club's women's facilities.

United's proposed new 100,000-seater stadium was included in the 2035 bid and could yet come under consideration from FIFA.

While there are still many hurdles to clear before then, hosting a tournament final in Manchester would undoubtedly be huge for the women's game, not least given the optics of a bid built around being 'all together', described as 'a rallying cry to unite people through football'.

London should not be the epicentre of the tournament, not if the intention is to spread the women's game across the United Kingdom rather than concentrate it in the capital, where Arsenal's attendances continue to dwarf those of every other WSL club.

In other words, the women's game in this country cannot be put on hold until 2035.

It cannot afford to wait eight-and-a-half years for this World Cup to come and rescue it. Time to get cracking.

#1485. Jack Grealish plays for Everton for the first time since being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline' - as winger comes off the bench during loss at Brentford

Published: 14:08 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:56 EST, 23 November 2026

Jack Grealish returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being made unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline, and came off the bench at half-time against Brentford on Monday.

The Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He had not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a 'breach of club discipline' and a lack of fitness thereafter.

He last featured on October 17, over a month ago, but returned to the match day squad to take on Brentford on Monday night – named on the substitutes' bench. He was introduced at half-time for Tyrique George, with the Toffees 2-0 down and down to 10 men after James Tarkowski's red card. They would ultimately lose 4-0.

Manager David Moyes said ahead of the game: 'He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

'We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don't want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn't be.'

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: 'He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?'

Jack Grealish (right) returned to Everton action on Monday for the first time since being punished for missing training

He was named on the bench against Brentford, coming on for Tyrique George at half-time

Everton had won their last three games and went into Monday's match sixth in the table. The result, though, was a blow as they dropped to ninth.

Asked what Grealish can offer, Moyes added: 'Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

'But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

'I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.'

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

#1483. Report: Andoni Iraola wants to bring versatile defensive sensation to Liverpool soon

Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool's manager has delivered a bit of a mixed bag of performances so far.

The Spaniard was brought in to replace Arne Slot after the Dutchman led his title-defending team to a fifth-place finish.

Clearly, this performance was nowhere near good enough for a title-defending team and, change was definitely needed.

And, even though over £150 million worth of change came through the Anfield doors in the summer, more deals need to be struck so that Liverpool can start competing for silverware again.

So, even though the transfer window isn't open yet, there's no reason for the rumour mill to not continue turning.

Liverpool are eyeing a move for Mohamed Simakan

Alongside Liverpool's attack, their defence has been a big problem for them.

Whether its been a lack of form or just the sheer number of injuries they've suffered, things just haven't gone to plan for Liverpool's back line over the last couple of years.

That's why players such as Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Giovanni Leoni have all been brought in.

Right now, things are in a good place for the Reds' back four but, that could all change if they choose against signing Araujo permanently.

Nothing is set in stone yet but, the fact that Caught Offside have shared that Mohamed Simakan is now wanted by Liverpool proves that Iraola and Julian Ward are trying to line up some back-up options just in case things don't go to plan.

"Liverpool and Manchester United are both monitoring Mohamed Simakan as the Premier League rivals consider defensive reinforcements ahead of 2027," they wrote.

"The 26-year-old has remained an important figure for Al-Nassr since leaving RB Leipzig and offers the kind of profile that could appeal to both clubs.

"Comfortable at centre-back or right-back, Simakan combines pace and physical strength with experience playing in an aggressive defensive system.

For Liverpool and United, however, January may be too early for anything concrete. For Liverpool, Simakan’s versatility is particularly attractive.

"With long-term succession planning required in central defence, signing a player capable of operating centrally while also covering right-back would give the squad valuable flexibility."

Mohamed Simakan could become Liverpool's next Ronald Araujo

One of the best things about Araujo is that he can comfortably play as a right-back or a centre-back.

No matter which position he's used in, he's always been seen as one of the Reds' best players this term with fans demanding that his deal is made permanent.

Clearly, this hasn't happened yet and, since rumours have been emerging that the price of Araujo would have to be slashed in half for Liverpool to even consider doing that, the deal doesn't feel all that likely to come to fruition.

This isn't ideal news but, the fact that Simakan can be used as a centre-back or a right-back does mean that change is coming to Anfield.

He may have spent the last couple of years in the Saudi Pro League with Al-Nassr but, he's still only 26 years old so, even if he isn't up to scratch right away, he could develop and become better.

Nothing is set in stone yet but, since Iraola wants to bring him in, Simakan could end up being a name that Liverpool's fans get rather used to.

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Spurs go close again! Solanke plays in Gallagher, who bundles his way into the six-yard box. Tielemans, Martinez and Yoro all fail to apprehend the Spurs midfielder, who digs a close-range shot out of his feet. However, Lammens is there to make a crucial block and thwart the visitors.

The visitors then steam forward again on the counter. On this occasion, Yoro defends magnificently, executing a well-timed sliding tackle on Van Hecke.

The visitors have made an excellent start to this game. Savio breezes past Maguire like he isn’t even there, but can’t quite find Kudus with his low cross. De Zerbi will want his side to capitalise on this dominant period. Man Utd look sluggish and asleep so far.

Gallagher receives an early yellow card after pulling Maguire back. Referee Attwell isn’t taking any prisoners. Man Utd supporters also show their love and appreciation for Rui Pinto with this banner.

Tottenham waste a huge chance! What is Lammens doing?! The Man Utd goalkeeper tries to pick out Mainoo with a very risky pass. It’s intercepted by Bergvall, who tees up Solanke. One-on-one with Lammens, the Spurs striker’s whipped effort is blocked by Lammens. The Belgian goes from zero to hero, emphatically redeeming himself.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Can either of these sides pick up a victory to relieve the pressure on their head coach?

“You cheating b******s, you know what you are,” is heard from the stands at Old Trafford. It’s pretty safe to say they are referring to Manchester City’s guilty verdict which was announced during the international break.

#1480. Columbus Crew vs Inter Miami - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:16, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:19

On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.

Columbus had a lot of momentum heading into the playoffs, and that continued on Saturday as they took advantage of some sloppy Miami defending to take a surprising lead in this series.

Laurent Courtois has seen his side score three or more goals in four of their last five matches versus MLS opposition, while posting a clean sheet in three of those instances, making them an appealing option to choose on the UK betting sites

The Crew exposed gaps in the Miami squad, scoring on three of their five targeted efforts last weekend and putting the Herons on the ropes heading into game two.

This is only the second time they are up 1-0 since this best-of-three first-round format was introduced, with this team advancing past Atlanta United in three games on the only previous occasion in which they were in this position in 2023.

Only once since their 2015 MLS Cup final defeat versus the Portland Timbers have they lost a post-season match at home, with the New York Red Bulls blanking them 1-0 in game one of that opening round series in 2024.

Friday will mark the second time the Crew can eliminate Miami from a major competition in Columbus, after knocking them out of the 2024 Leagues Cup thanks to a 3-2 victory at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in the round of 16.

For a team boasting so much experience and talent in the biggest club and international competitions, Inter Miami failed to keep their composure in numerous instances last weekend.

Saturday’s defeat was the joint-worst for the club in the post-season, though given everything that transpired, they could be looking much worse heading into this match.

Kily Gonzalez will be relieved to know that Lionel Messi is available, escaping with just a caution in game one after throwing the ball at Gonzalo Tapia, a moment some believed should have warranted a sending off for the Argentine.

Miami played a good portion of that match a man down, and have never won the second game in a best-of-three MLS playoff series.

The Herons have given up a combined six goals in their last two matches versus MLS opposition and have yet to beat an MLS club in a knockout fixture this season.

The reigning league champions have lost four of their five all-time playoff outings away from home, with their only triumph coming at FC Cincinnati in 2025 (4-0).

Due to a cruciate ligament tear, Wessam Abou Ali will not be available for Columbus in game two of this series.

Gonzalo Tapia netted twice in Miami, with Taha Habroune also scoring as Patrick Schulte made three stops for the clean sheet.

On the Miami side, Mateo Silvetti is dealing with a shoulder issue, Tadeo Allende still has a knee problem and Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Gonzalo Lujan will be suspended following his red card in game one, while Sergio Reguilon, David Ayala and Cesar Abadia are all questionable with lower-body injuries.

#1478. Five Man United players who could leave in January as part of major Mauricio Pochettino clear-out

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 14:30, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:32

Manchester United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, with the club potentially making three mid-season signings.

The Red Devils currently find themselves down in 19th spot in the Premier League table and facing what would be a stunning relegation from the top flight.

There could also be first-team departures in the winter market, as new head coach Mauricio Pochettino begins to shape the squad.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five players who could potentially leave Old Trafford when the January market opens for business.

Zirkzee was linked with a move away from Man United over the summer, but he was ultimately not allowed to depart due to the fact that the Red Devils were unable to sign a replacement.

Even with Benjamin Sesko out injured, Zirkzee has not started a single match this season, with each of his 11 appearances coming off the bench.

The Netherlands international has scored twice this season, but his overall record for Man United since arriving from Bologna in 2024 is 11 goals in 86 appearances.

It has been a struggle for the 25-year-old in English football, but he is not short of interest, and a return to Serie A in January is seen as a serious possibility at this stage.

Como and Napoli are the latest clubs to be linked with Zirkzee.

Mazraoui is reportedly attracting the attention of AC Milan ahead of the January market, with a mid-season departure for the Morocco international thought to be possible.

The 29-year-old has underperformed in his nine appearances for Man United this season and is not believed to be in the club's long-term plans.

Initially, the defender impressed after arriving from Bayern Munich, and he has now represented the Red Devils on 86 occasions in all competitions.

However, a switch in the January market could be on the cards, especially if Man United are able to boost their options at full-back in the winter window.

Heaven is reportedly open to the idea of leaving Man United during the winter market.

The 20-year-old has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool in the team's last match, which ended in a 4-0 defeat.

Man United are expected to bring in a new centre-back in January, and Heaven is said to be concerned over what that would mean for his playing time.

As a result, the Englishman is allegedly open to a winter loan move, while a permanent exit is not being ruled out depending on what offers arrive.

Heaven, who has a contract with Man United until the summer of 2029, has made 32 appearances for the club since arriving from Arsenal in February 2025.

Martinez's contract with Man United is due to expire at the end of the campaign, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough season for the Argentine.

A new deal for the 28-year-old is seen as highly unlikely given that he has openly criticised Man United chiefs, such as director of football Jason Wilcox, during the 2026-27 season.

Man United will be reluctant to lose the Argentina international on a free transfer, so it is possible that a sale in the January window could occur, depending on the offer.

Martinez has been one of the team's biggest under-performers this season, and it appears that his time at Old Trafford will come to an end at some stage in 2027.

Amass may yet be given the chance to prove himself to new Man United head coach Pochettino, but the defender's future looks to be away from Old Trafford.

The 19-year-old was heavily linked with a departure during the summer window, but he stayed at Man United past the deadline and has made two appearances this season, both in the Champions League.

Amass was not in the squad against Liverpool last time out, though, and Luke Shaw's return to fitness has pushed him further down the pecking order.

A number of Championship clubs are believed to be keen on the teenager, who only has a deal with the 20-time English champions until the end of the season.

#1477. GdS: Unbeaten and hope or room for error – Milan begin Europa League calculations

AC Milan have four games left to play in the Europa League and they’re in the do-or-die stage of the competition already.

Thoughts on the Europa League this season were mixed. On paper, Milan should have been competing at the top. Yet, they’ve struggled through the League Phase so far, leaving themselves with something of a mountain to climb, starting against Olympiacos later this week.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are in a more-than-difficult position. Sitting 28th in the rankings, they are currently outside the qualification spots and calculations are difficult to make about how much they’ll need to improve.

In Greece, they’ll face the first hurdle and getting three points would make life much easier for everyone involved.

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:36

Real Salt Lake will try to extend their season into next week with a Friday win over the Vancouver Whitecaps at America First Field in game two of that best-of-three playoff series.

The reigning MLS Cup runners-up captured game one 2-0 last Sunday, putting them one win away from round two in the Western Conference playoffs.

After surviving a nervy shootout in the Wild Card Round, Salt Lake are now on the brink of elimination yet again after a subpar showing in game one against the Caps.

On Sunday, Pablo Mastroeni’s men suffered just their second defeat in their last eight MLS outings and were second-best for much of the game.

While they are on the verge of another early exit, they can draw optimism from being unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs at America First Field.

During the regular season, Salt Lake showed strong attacking potency on home soil, netting three or more goals six times and scoring multiple times on 12 separate occasions.

They will try to end a five-match playoff losing run on Friday, scoring a goal or fewer in each of those instances.

Claret and Cobalt have not lost a playoff match at home in 90 minutes this decade, with their only such victory at America First Field occurring on penalties versus the Houston Dynamo in game two of that opening round series.

It is just one game, but Vancouver looked very much like title contenders as they began the 2026 MLS post-season in style.

Jesper Sorensen’s side carried the play throughout game one and will seek a fifth consecutive MLS triumph on Friday.

While this is the fourth straight year the Caps are in the post-season, they have won only once in that span in normal time away from home, beating San Diego 3-1 in the Western Conference Final last year.

Meanwhile, they failed to win three of their final four regular-season away fixtures this season against Western Conference opposition, with the highest-scoring team in the West failing to score on two of those occasions.

Vancouver have never lost a playoff encounter under Sorensen when netting first but have also never won a post-season outing in 90 minutes when conceding the opener under his leadership.

Sorensen, meanwhile, has won every match against RSL as the Caps boss, including their last two visits to America First Field, in which his team scored three goals both times.

Vancouver Whitecaps Major League Soccer form:

Due to a hamstring strain, Ariath Piol may miss this match for RSL, while Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are questionable because of knee injuries and Zach Booth still has to clear concussion protocol.

Sergi Solans has scored three goals in his last two MLS home outings, including the opener in their 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Galaxy on Decision Day, while Rafael Cabral kept game one close, making six saves, many of them spectacular.

On the Vancouver side, an illness may keep Belal Halbouni out on Friday, and it is unlikely we will see Kenji Cabrera feature as he deals with a foot injury.

Edier Ocampo got the Caps on the board late in the opening half of game one, with Bruno Caicedo adding some insurance in the final 45 minutes.

#1475. IT'S A GAME CHANGER! Scotland to co-host Women's World Cup with England, Northern Ireland and Wales in 2035

Published: 13:05 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 23 November 2026

Scotland, England, Northern Ireland and Wales have been confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

It will be the first men’s or women’s World Cup finals to be staged in the UK since the 1966 men’s tournament was held in England.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland (Hampden and Easter Road) and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams.

A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea stadium – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 stadiums across the four nations.

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold.

Joy for Spain after they defeated England in the 2023 Women's World Cup final

Scotland captain Caroline Weir says the World Cup will take the nation's game to another level

FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

For England this represents another chance to host a major women’s tournament, having hosted the European Championship in 2022 which the Lionesses won.

The Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: 'The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

'Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep – and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.'

FIFA president Gianni Infantino announces the home nations as World Cup hosts

Scotland captain Caroline Weir added: 'The women’s game in Scotland has so much potential and this tournament is a real opportunity to drive momentum and help take it to another level both nationally and internationally.

'We’re so proud to play our part in welcoming the world in 2035 and I know I speak on behalf of all of the players and staff when I say that we are ready to rise to the challenge and help deliver a truly memorable, world-class tournament.'

England forward Michelle Agyemang said it was 'incredibly special' and added: 'I’ve been lucky enough to know what it feels like to play for my country in a major tournament, and those are moments you dream about as a young girl playing football.

'The thought of another generation growing up knowing that the biggest stage in the game is coming to their home country is amazing. To have the chance to play in a home World Cup would be a dream, but even more exciting is thinking about all the girls watching who might see 2035 and believe they can be part of it one day.'

SFA chief Ian Maxwell says tournament will be 'most significant thing to happen to women's and girls' game in Scotland'

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be 'the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland'.

He said: 'The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.'

First Minister John Swinney said: 'This is fantastic news for Scotland. We have proved time and again that we are a world-class host, and I am delighted that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035 will be held in Scotland alongside England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

'The timing is ideal. Project 2035, our new long-term plan to grow the girls’ and women’s game, aims to establish Scotland as a leading nation for women’s football by 2035. Our newly established girls’ and women’s football taskforce will help to make this happen, capitalising on the World Cup and leaving a lasting legacy for communities across the country.

'Scotland is building a remarkable reputation for hosting major events, and the FIFA Women’s World Cup joins the Tour de France Grand Départ, The Open, the World Rally Championships and UEFA EURO 2028 in promising to showcase what our country has to offer. We will make sure each one of these amazing sporting events delivers for our economy, supporting jobs, businesses and tourism.'

#1471. Maritimo vs Nacional - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 25 Nov 2026 16:48

Maritimo and Nacional renew their Madeira derby rivalry in the Primeira Liga on Friday evening, with both sides looking to claim an important victory and move further clear of the drop zone.

The two clubs are meeting in the top flight for the first time in five years, with the visitors sitting 13th in the Primeira Liga table on 10 points from 11 matches, just two points above the 15th-placed hosts, who have a game in hand against Estoril Praia and sit outside the relegation playoff place on head-to-head points ahead of Casa Pia.

Maritimo made an encouraging start to life back in the top flight, winning their opening two league fixtures against Casa Pia and Famalicao, but they have not claimed another Primeira Liga victory since beating the latter on August 16.

Mitchell van der Gaag's side have since gone eight league matches without a win (D2, L6), including defeats in their last three such outings against Porto (2-1), Vitoria de Guimaraes (5-0) and Santa Clara (2-0).

Only bottom-placed Estoril, who are yet to win a league match this season, have endured a longer winless run, while Maritimo have scored the third-fewest goals in the division (nine) and conceded the third-most (21).

Van der Gaag's men have also struggled to make home advantage count, recording just one victory from five league matches at their own ground and losing the last three, during which they conceded multiple goals on each occasion and scored just once.

Maritimo did, however, receive a welcome boost in the Taca de Portugal last weekend, progressing past Chaves following a goalless draw and a 3-2 penalty shootout victory, and will hope that result provides some momentum ahead of Friday's derby.

Nacional have also endured a difficult start to the campaign, but they have collected six points from their last three matches, including a 1-0 victory over Academico de Viseu courtesy of Matchoi Djalo's late winner.

That result marked the first victory under new boss Joao Henriques, who arrived in late October as the club's third permanent manager of the season following the departures of Joao Giao and Alexandre Santos.

Henriques initially struggled to build on interim coach Bruno Abreu's home victory over Braga, losing away to Arouca in his first match in charge, but the latest success has given the Alvinegros an opportunity to record consecutive competitive wins for the first time since beating Alverca and Tondela in April.

Interestingly, Nacional's last four matches have each produced just one goal, including their disappointing Taca de Portugal defeat to lower-division Sanjoanense on October 17, meaning taking maximum points on Friday could hinge on greater efficiency in attack and defensive discipline.

However, the Islanders still have plenty of room for improvement away from home, having collected just one point from five Primeira Liga trips this season, drawing at Santa Clara on the opening weekend before losing their next four against Vitoria, Sporting, Rio Ave and Arouca.

Nacional have also found this fixture difficult in recent meetings, losing four of their last five league encounters with Maritimo across the Primeira Liga and Liga 2 (D1), including a 3-1 defeat on their most recent competitive visit.

Maritimo are monitoring defenders Rafael Fernandes (muscle) and Paulo Henrique (thigh), who both missed last weekend's cup tie against Chaves.

Yellu Santiago is also working his way back to full fitness from an injury, having only featured in the opening weekend of the Primeira Liga campaign.

Goncal Tabuaco's performance against Chaves has given Van der Gaag a decision to make in goal after he replaced Fran Vieites in the cup, saving two penalties during the shootout.

Nacional will be without Ulisses Wilson and Filipe Soares, who are both recovering from ankle injuries and remain unavailable.

Leo Santos (knee) is also sidelined, while Brazilian duo Wesley Gasolina and Liziero continue to recover from their respective injuries.

Henriques could retain the lineup that started against Viseu, with Miguel Baeza anchoring the midfield, although Djalo is pushing for a starting place after making an impact from the bench last time out.

Vieites; Igor Juliao, Correia, Szalai; Tavares, Andrade, Guzzo, Ogbeta; Bassouamina, Butzke Tejon

Marin; Jensen, Goncalves, Vitor, Kokolo; Baeza, Dias, Djalo; Labidi, Njoya, Song

Maritimo have struggled to turn home advantage into league points this season, but Nacional's poor away record gives the hosts reason to believe they can avoid defeat, making a share of the spoils a reasonable prediction.
